newsitem.title: USA: New York Senate re-elects Bruno as Majority Leader.
newsitem.headline: New York Senate re-elects Bruno as Majority Leader.

text.p: The Republican-controlled New York State Senate on Tuesday said it re-elected Joseph Bruno (R-Troy) to fill a second term as the Majority Leader.

Bruno, in prepared remarks, said that in the next two years, the challenges facing the state include approving welfare reforms and cutting property taxes, utility rates and the costs of doing business in New York.
At the same time, Martin Connor, D-Manhattan, was relected to a second term as the Senate Minority Leader.

In prepared remarks that suggested Democrats, who control the Assembly, might oppose some of the new welfare reforms that were proposed by Gov George Pataki, Connor said "Our twin priorities must be jobs and compassionate common sense."
